newsitem.title: USA: Bondholders sue Los Angeles over development - paper.
newsitem.headline: Bondholders sue Los Angeles over development - paper.

text.p: Bondholders who invested $13.4 million in a housing project in downtown Los Angeles have sued the city and the project developer to recover their investments, the Los Angeles Times reported Thursday.
The suit, which names the city of Los Angeles, the city's housing authority and developer Thomas Bell, alleged fraud, negligence, conspiracy and breach of official duty, the newspaper reported.
The Hayward Manor project, a 525-unit single residence occupancy hotel, was part of a $110 million development plan to create affordable housing in the city.
In 1992, Bell and several other investors received $10 million in city housing development money and nearly $13.4 million of housing authority revenue bond funds to acquire and renovate the complex.

The development partnership defaulted on the loans last year, prompting the bondholder lawsuit, the Times reported. Bondholders alleged in the suit that the city was negligent in its management of the project.
Bell's attorney, Donald Etra, was not immediately available for comment. He told the Times that Bell was "innocent of all allegations of any wrongdoing whatsoever pertaining to the project."
